classification.difficultyReason: Part a chains the tangent-radius right angles, the quadrilateral sum for the central angle, and the half-angle at the circumference. Part b chains the right angle, the central angle, and the half angle. Each needs several linked circle theorems with no signposting.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=360^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ-48^\circ\\&=132^\circ\\a&=\frac{132^\circ}{2}\\&=66^\circ\end{align*}$$
Here $\theta$ is the centre angle between the two points of contact. Each tangent is perpendicular to its radius, and the angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc.

The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-32^\circ\\&=58^\circ\\\phi&=180^\circ-58^\circ\\&=122^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-122^\circ}{2}\\&=29^\circ\end{align*}$$
Here $\theta$ is the centre angle facing the external point and $\phi$ faces the far endpoint of the chord. The triangle formed by the two radii is isosceles.
